Forearms Exercises

Your forearms control the wrist and fingers, so they are involved whenever you grip a bar, dumbbell or handle. Strong forearms help you hold heavier weights for rows, pull-ups and deadlifts, and they add visible size to the arm.

📍 Between the elbow and wrist 4–10 sets/week

Anatomy

The forearm has a flexor group on the palm side that closes the hand and flexes the wrist, and an extensor group on the back that opens the hand and extends the wrist. The brachioradialis is a large forearm muscle that helps bend the elbow, especially with a neutral or overhand grip.

Function

Wrist flexion and extension, forearm rotation and gripping

Min Sets/Week
4
Optimal Range
4–10
Max Sets/Week
10

Training Tips

  • Most people get plenty of forearm work from heavy pulling; add direct work if grip limits your lifts.
  • Train the extensors (reverse wrist curls) as well as the flexors for balance.
  • Carries and heavy holds build grip endurance that wrist curls do not.

Where forearms fits in a workout split

You can train forearms in a push pull legs, upper/lower split or the bro split. Not sure which suits your schedule? Use the Split Finder, or see how weekly sets stack up in the workout planner.

FAQ

How often should I train forearms?▾
Most people benefit from training forearms 2 times per week. This provides enough frequency for muscle protein synthesis while allowing adequate recovery between sessions.
How many sets per week for forearms?▾
4–10 working sets per week is a reasonable range for most trainees. Start at the lower end and increase gradually as your recovery allows.
What is the best exercise for forearms?▾
The best exercise depends on your equipment and goals. For overall development, wrist curl is typically one of the most effective choices.
